edge_explainer: Ouster is the one name in this cohort where the business genuinely got better and the queue's premise is out of date. Revenue grew 49% year over year, gross margin expanded to 42.8%, the loss narrowed, the term debt was retired in 2024, and the share count now grows about 10% a year on stock compensation rather than the SPAC-era death spiral the note describes — $173 million of cash against a $7 million quarterly burn is a multi-year runway. None of that makes it ownable at this price. Sixteen times trailing sales for a hardware company with a negative 40% operating margin and no disclosed date for making money is a narrative multiple, and lidar carries structural ASP deflation that puts the margin expansion and the volume growth in direct tension. The path check settles it: the stock is up 73% from a low set 58 sessions ago, up another 9% today, and reports in three days — the run has front-run its own catalyst. This is a price rejection rather than a business rejection, so a price gate is the right instrument in principle, but the gate sits 45-55% below spot. It is also not shortable: beta 3.3, thin promotional coverage and nineteen ten-percent days this year is squeeze fuel.
